newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Scor says ready for NYK listing.
newsitem.headline: French Scor says ready for NYK listing.

text.p: France's leading reinsurer, Scor, said on Friday it was ready for its debut on Wall Street and was awaiting the green light from U.S. stock market authorities.

"Everything is pretty well ready. We can go when the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) gives us the go-ahead and if market conditions are good," Scor chairman Jacques Blondeau told a news conference.
"Everything seems to be pretty well in place for this to be carried out in a relatively short time."
He made the comments after the company announced half-year profits rose 40 percent to 288 million francs and was upbeat about full-year prospects, forecasting this "will definitely be a good year".
The company annonced in June it planned to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange to broaden its shareholder base.
Blondeau said the listing should occur this autumn, probably in September, and would not be accompanied by any capital increase.

The shares offered to the U.S. market would nearly all be from the disposal by UAP of a "substantial" portion of its 40.9 percent stake in the reinsurer. An industry source said that UAP's stake in Scor should fall to around 10 percent.
Axa announced last week that it had completed the sale of its 9.7 percent stake. AGF is only keeping a symbolic holding of 0.7 percent after having sold nine percent since it was privatised in June.
Axa, which owns reinsurer Axa Re and AGF, which owns Safr reinsurer had long wished to dispose of their stakes in Scor which they no longer considered to be strategic holdings.
Their Scor shares were largely sold into the market.

Predica, a life insurance unit of Credit Agricole bought up some two percent of the shares and a German investment fund bought between two and less than five percent, a Scor official said. The group Societe Suisse France took 2.25 percent of Scor from AGF.
Scor said it planned to add to its portfolio but pay lower prices than it had in the past.
Scor shares were unchanged at 212 francs at 1228 GMT. Its shares have risen nearly 40 percent since the start of the year.
